'''Alex Eskin''' ({{Langx|ru|Александр Григорьевич Эскин}}, born May 19, 1965)<ref name=CV>[https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~eskin/vitae.pdf Alex Eskin, Curriculum Vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712072001/http://math.uchicago.edu/~eskin/vitae.pdf |date=July 12, 2019 }}, Department of Mathematics, [[University of Chicago]]. Accessed September 7, 2019</ref> is an American mathematician. He is the Arthur Holly Compton distinguished service professor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="Lerner">{{cite web|author=Louise Lerner|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/uchicago-mathematician-physicists-win-3-million-oscars-science|title=UChicago mathematician, physicists win $3 million 'Oscars of science'|work=UChicago News, [[University of Chicago]]|date=September 6, 2019|access-date=September 7, 2019}} </ref> His research focuses on [[Dynamical billiards|rational billiards]] and [[geometric group theory]].

==Biography==
Eskin was born in [[Kiev]] on May 19, 1965.<ref name="Lerner"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/alex-eskin-w8xzel/|title=Alex Eskin. Member profile.|work=[[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=September 10, 2019}} </ref> He is the son of a Russian-Jewish mathematician [[Gregory Eskin|Gregory I. Eskin]],{{cn|date=September 2019}} a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. The family emigrated to Israel in 1974 and in 1982 to the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/sites/default/files/newsletter/nl2016.pdf|title=The After Math|page=6|magazine=The Common Denominator|date=Fall 2016|publisher=UCLA Department of Mathematics}}</ref>

Eskin earned his doctorate from [[Princeton University]] in 1993, under the supervision of [[Peter Sarnak]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=53170 }}</ref>

Eskin has been a professor at the [[University of Chicago]] since 1999.<ref name="UC"/>

==Awards==
Eskin gave invited talks at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin in 1998,<ref>{{cite book|author=Eskin, Alex|chapter=Counting problems and semisimple groups|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=539–552|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011691000}}</ref> and in [[Hyderabad]] in 2010.<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=eskin ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers], [[International Mathematical Union]]. Accessed September 7, 2019.</ref>

For his contribution to joint work with [[David Fisher (mathematician)|David Fisher]] and [[Kevin Whyte]] establishing the [[Quasi-isometry|quasi-isometric]] rigidity of solvable groups, Eskin was awarded the 2007 [[Clay Research Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.claymath.org/research |work=[[Clay Mathematics Institute]]|title=Clay Research Award.  |access-date=June 25, 2019}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved December 2, 2012.</ref> In April 2015, Eskin was elected a member of the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="UC">{{cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/article/2015/05/05/mathematician-alex-eskin-two-alumni-elected-national-academy-sciences |title=Mathematician Alex Eskin, two alumni elected to National Academy of Sciences|publisher= UChicagoNews|date=May 5, 2015 |access-date =November 20, 2015}}</ref><ref>[http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-28-2015-NAS-Election.html National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151120211335/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-28-2015-NAS-Election.html |date=November 20, 2015 }}, [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]], April 28, 2015; accessed November 20, 2015</ref> Eskin won the 2020 [[Breakthrough Prize]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.livescience.com/breakthrough-prize-mathematics-2019-winners.html|work=[[Live Science]]|title=Mathematician Wins $3 Million Breakthrough Prize for 'Magic Wand Theorem'|author= Rafi Letzter|date=September 5, 2019|access-date=September 7, 2019}} </ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/54|title=Breakthrough Prize – Winners Of The 2020 Breakthrough Prize In Life Sciences, Fundamental Physics And Mathematics Announced|website=breakthroughprize.org}}</ref> in mathematics for his classification of <math>P</math>-invariant and stationary measures for the moduli of translation surfaces,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Invariant and stationary measures for the action on Moduli space|first1=Alex|last1=Eskin|first2=Maryam|last2=Mirzakhani|date=June 7, 2018|journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS|volume=127|issue=1|pages=95–324|doi=10.1007/s10240-018-0099-2|s2cid=119906170}}</ref> in joint work with [[Maryam Mirzakhani]].
